# HubScoreResult { #dyf.HubScoreResult }

```python
HubScoreResult(
    scores,
    eigenvector,
    distance_to_center,
    eigenvector_z,
    distance_z,
)
```

Result of hub score computation.

Hub nodes are structural centers that hold the embedding space together.
They are characterized by:
- High eigenvector centrality (in tightly woven neighborhoods)
- Low distance to global centroid (central position in space)

Unlike PageRank, which rewards being pointed to by many nodes (both categories
AND popular instances qualify), eigenvector centrality rewards being in a
tightly interconnected cluster. Abstract concepts cluster more tightly than
popular instances.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name               | Type                                     | Description                                                 |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| scores             | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Hub score for each point (higher = more structural/general) |
| eigenvector        | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Eigenvector centrality for each point                       |
| distance_to_center | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Distance to global centroid for each point                  |
| eigenvector_z      | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Z-scored eigenvector centrality                             |
| distance_z         | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Z-scored distance to center                                 |

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [get_hub_nodes](#dyf.HubScoreResult.get_hub_nodes) | Return indices of nodes with hub score above threshold. |
| [get_top_hubs](#dyf.HubScoreResult.get_top_hubs) | Return indices of top k hub nodes. |

### get_hub_nodes { #dyf.HubScoreResult.get_hub_nodes }

```python
HubScoreResult.get_hub_nodes(threshold=0.0)
```

Return indices of nodes with hub score above threshold.

### get_top_hubs { #dyf.HubScoreResult.get_top_hubs }

```python
HubScoreResult.get_top_hubs(k=100)
```

Return indices of top k hub nodes.
